title: Investor Profiling Questionnaire
description: Current Chainlit questionnaire aligned to the single-choice items from Barita SOC(2). Numeric and free-text items from the DOCX are still deferred in this chat flow.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of this portfolio?
questions.help_text: This captures what the money is mainly meant to support.

options.label: To make a major purchase
options.description: The money may be needed for a specific future expense.

options.label: To save for retirement
options.description: The portfolio is aimed at future retirement needs.

options.label: To build long-term wealth
options.description: The main goal is long-term capital growth.

options.label: Other goal
options.description: The purpose does not fit neatly into the listed categories.

questions.text: What is the time horizon for this goal?
questions.help_text: This helps show how much time the portfolio has to recover from market swings.

questions.text: Which age range are you in?
questions.help_text: This is one of the risk-capacity signals in the current draft questionnaire.

questions.text: How stable is your income outside this portfolio?
questions.help_text: This helps estimate how dependent you are on the portfolio for near-term needs.

options.label: Somewhat stable
options.description: Income is present but not perfectly consistent.

questions.text: Which phase of your investment life best fits you right now?
questions.help_text: This is the DOCX income-versus-growth question phrased for direct chat use.

options.label: Capital accumulation
options.description: The focus is still mainly on growth.

options.label: Capital disbursement
options.description: The focus is more on drawing income or spending from assets.

questions.text: Over the next 12-24 months, what share of this portfolio do you expect to withdraw for major expenses?
questions.help_text: The DOCX mentions house, education, and lifestyle expenses here. The live chat uses a percentage bucket instead of a numeric input for now.

questions.text: How many months of essential expenses do you already have set aside for emergencies?
questions.help_text: This is one of the DOCX liquidity-capacity questions.

questions.text: How willing are you to take financial risk or lose money in this portfolio?
questions.help_text: This is the direct risk-tolerance question from the DOCX.

options.label: Very low
options.description: Very little willingness to accept losses.

options.label: High
options.description: Comfortable with a meaningful level of risk.

questions.text: When holding risky assets, which preference fits you best?
questions.help_text: This asks whether you lean more toward safety or return when risk is involved.

questions.text: How knowledgeable are you about financial and investment concepts?
questions.help_text: This is asked directly in the DOCX risk-tolerance section.

options.label: Not at all knowledgeable
options.description: Very limited familiarity with finance and investing.

questions.text: How much experience do you have with investment products?
questions.help_text: This is still single-choice in the live chat version.

questions.text: What is your opinion of the stock market?
questions.help_text: This reflects how risky or safe the investor perceives the market to be.

options.label: Very risky
options.description: The stock market feels highly dangerous.

options.label: Somewhat risky
options.description: The market still feels risky overall.

options.label: Neutral
options.description: No strong positive or negative view.

options.label: Very safe
options.description: The market feels comfortable and safe.

questions.text: In the past, when faced with investment losses, what action did you take?
questions.help_text: This is the final behavioral loss-tolerance question from the DOCX.

options.label: Purchased more
options.description: Added to the investment after prices fell.
